GeneralGuidance: Use a broad-spectrum fungicide (e.g. copper-based, triazole, or strobilurin class — ask your local agri store which brand they carry). Fungal diseases spread fast in humid weather, so early action matters.
Timing: Apply early morning or late evening (avoid midday heat/sun). Repeat every 7-14 days if disease persists, or as per product label.
Precautions: Wear gloves and mask. Do not spray before rain (washes off). Keep children and animals away from treated area for 24 hours.

GeneralGuidance: Copper-based bactericides are commonly used for bacterial crop diseases. Remove and destroy severely infected plant parts to stop spread.
Timing: Apply at first sign of symptoms. Avoid overhead irrigation which spreads bacteria through water splash.
Precautions: Bacterial diseases spread through water and tools — disinfect tools between plants. Copper products should not be overused as it can build up in soil.

GeneralGuidance: There is no chemical cure for viral plant diseases. Focus on removing infected plants to stop spread, and controlling insect vectors (aphids, whiteflies, leafhoppers) that carry the virus.
Timing: Act immediately upon identifying a viral infection — remove infected plants.
Precautions: Use insecticides only to control the insect vector, not the virus itself. Always sanitize tools and hands after handling infected plants.

GeneralGuidance: Use a targeted insecticide appropriate for the specific pest, or consider neem-oil based organic options for lower toxicity.
Timing: Apply in early morning or evening when beneficial insects (bees) are less active.
Precautions: Avoid spraying during flowering to protect pollinators. Rotate insecticide types to prevent pest resistance.

GeneralGuidance: This disease type needs specific diagnosis. Please consult your local agriculture extension officer before treatment.
Precautions: Always read the product label fully before use.
